questions.scenario: It's time for the famous 'Onion Peel' Biology practical in your school lab. What do you enjoy the most?

options.text: Carefully staining the peel with pink safranin, placing the glass coverslip without bubbles, and adjusting the microscope lens.
Observing the cell structure and memorizing the exact functions of the nucleus, cytoplasm, and vacuoles from the textbook.
Drawing a neat, perfectly shaded diagram of the cell in your practical file using an HB pencil.
Helping the teacher distribute the microscopes to groups, organizing the slides, and ensuring the lab stays disciplined.

questions.scenario: You go to a local pathology lab (like Dr. Lal PathLabs) for a routine blood test. What catches your attention?

options.text: Watching the phlebotomist carefully extract the blood and load the colorful test tubes into the spinning centrifuge machine.
Staring at the final printed report, matching your Hemoglobin and WBC count numbers with the 'normal reference range'.
Looking at the colorful posters on the clinic wall that show cool, 3D diagrams of red blood cells fighting bacteria.
Wondering how many patients visit daily and calculating how much profit the lab makes on a standard Dengue or Malaria test.

questions.scenario: You are watching an episode of CID where Dr. Salunkhe solves a murder case. What is the coolest part?

options.text: Imagining yourself wearing gloves, pouring glowing chemicals into glass flasks, and physically extracting fingerprints.
Loving the part where they run the DNA sequence through the computer database to find the exact percentage match of the killer.
Being fascinated by the 3D computer animation on the screen showing how the poison actually entered the victim's bloodstream.
Thinking about how Dr. Salunkhe manages the entire forensic lab, orders high-tech equipment, and guides his team of assistants.

questions.scenario: You are reading news articles about viruses and vaccines (like Covaxin or Covishield). What fascinates you?

options.text: How scientists actually handle dangerous live viruses wearing full PPE suits inside highly secure, sanitized glass cabinets.
The statistical data on efficacy rates, sample sizes, and how the virus RNA mutates into new genetic variants.
Looking at those spiky, glowing 3D graphics of the virus on TV news channels and wishing you could design them.
Thinking about how Indian pharma companies scaled up massive factory production to supply crores of vaccines worldwide.

questions.scenario: A family member gets prescribed a new capsule medicine by the doctor. What do you do?

options.text: Open one capsule just to see the tiny powder granules inside and wonder how they physically dissolve in stomach acid.
Read the tiny instruction paper inside the box to check the chemical composition, dosage metrics, and side effects.
Admire the shiny packaging, the cool logo of the pharma company, and the color coding of the blister pack.
Check the MRP on the back and wonder how much margin the local chemist makes compared to the giant manufacturing company.

questions.scenario: Your school takes you on an industrial visit to a local dairy plant like Amul or Mother Dairy. What is your focus?

options.text: Checking out the massive pasteurization tanks and the exact physical process of culturing bacteria to make curd.
Asking the guide about the temperature algorithms and exact fat percentage formulas used to grade the milk quality.
Staring at the vibrant mascots, packaging designs, and catchy ad campaigns painted on the factory walls.
Observing the factory manager coordinating the massive supply chain of milk trucks arriving from villages.

questions.scenario: You are studying Human Genetics and Heredity in your 10th Standard Science textbook. What is your reaction?

options.text: Wanting to actually extract real DNA from a banana or onion at home using dish soap, salt, and rubbing alcohol.
Obsessing over solving the 'Punnett square' math puzzles to figure out if an offspring will have brown or blue eyes.
Marveling at the beautiful, twisted double-helix shape of the DNA and sketching it perfectly in the margins of your notebook.
Realizing that advanced DNA ancestry testing kits could become a massive, highly profitable startup business in India.

questions.scenario: You stumble upon a random YouTube video explaining 'Genetically Modified Crops' in farming. Which part hooks you?

options.text: Watching scientists physically use microscopic glass needles to inject new DNA directly into a plant cell.
Understanding the complex genetic code and how specific DNA segments are 'cut and pasted' like computer programming.
Getting captivated by the bright, colorful 3D animations explaining how a tomato was altered to look redder and plumper.
Watching the segment on how an agriculture startup created pest-resistant cotton seeds and sold them to thousands of farmers.

questions.scenario: Mummy brings a new, expensive 'anti-aging' Vitamin C face serum. What do you do?

options.text: Want to put a drop under your school microscope to see if it really contains the 'active fruit enzymes' it claims.
Turn the bottle to read the exact percentage of Hyaluronic Acid and Google the scientific research behind what it does to skin.
Love the sleek, frosted glass bottle, the premium dropper, and the beautiful typography used on the label.
Explain to Mummy that she fell for a clever marketing trick and calculate how overpriced the tiny 30ml bottle actually is.

questions.scenario: It's the annual Inter-School Science Fair and your team chooses a Biotechnology topic. What is your role?

options.text: You build the actual working model of a bioreactor using plastic bottles, pipes, and yeast to show fermentation.
You create a detailed chart with data graphs explaining how gene therapy can cure specific hereditary diseases.
You make an incredibly beautiful, massive thermocol model of a human brain or a virus that wins the 'Best Display' award.
You are the team leader who decided the topic, sourced the cheap materials from the local market, and pitched the idea to the judges.

Lab_Technician.title: The Lab Warrior (Clinical Tech / Researcher)
Lab_Technician.primary_match_text: You are a hands-on explorer! You love practical experiments, getting into the details, and physically interacting with the microscopic world.
Lab_Technician.day_in_the_life: Wearing a lab coat, preparing DNA samples, operating high-tech microscopes, and discovering the hidden bacteria or cells causing diseases.
Lab_Technician.alternative_match_text: Your love for hands-on science makes you a great fit for fields like Pharmacy, Forensic Science, or Food Technology.
Lab_Technician.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Science (PCB/PCMB). Entrance Exam: CUET or State Level Exams. Degree: B.Sc in Biotechnology, Microbiology, or B.Sc Medical Lab Technology (MLT).

Bioinformatics_Analyst.title: The Gene Coder (Bioinformatics Analyst / Geneticist)
Bioinformatics_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are the logic master! You realize that biology isn't just about drawing diagrams; it's about data, complex genetic codes, and solving the puzzle of DNA.
Bioinformatics_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Sitting at a high-end computer, running Python code to analyze billions of DNA sequences, and figuring out how genes cause human diseases.
Bioinformatics_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your analytical brain and love for tech make you an amazing fit for Data Science, Software Engineering, or Biostatistics.
Bioinformatics_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Science (PCM/PCB with Computer Science). Entrance Exam: JEE Mains, NEET, or CUET. Degree: B.Tech or B.Sc in Bioinformatics or Genetics.

Medical_Illustrator.title: The Bio-Artist (Medical Illustrator / 3D Designer)
Medical_Illustrator.primary_match_text: You have a beautiful blend of art and science! You love the visual beauty of nature and possess the creativity to explain complex biology through stunning graphics.
Medical_Illustrator.day_in_the_life: Designing 3D animations of viruses for medical textbooks, sketching human anatomy for educational apps, and making science look breathtaking.
Medical_Illustrator.alternative_match_text: Your creative superpower would also make you a brilliant Graphic Designer, Animator, or UI/UX Designer.
Medical_Illustrator.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Science (PCB preferred) or Arts/Humanities. Entrance Exam: UCEED or NID. Degree: B.Des (Bachelor of Design), B.F.A (Fine Arts), or B.Sc Animation.

Biotech_Manager.title: The R&D Visionary (Biotech Entrepreneur / Manager)
Biotech_Manager.primary_match_text: You are a born leader with a business mind! You want to take amazing scientific discoveries out of the lab and turn them into products that can save millions of lives.
Biotech_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing a team of brilliant scientists, securing multi-crore funding for a new vaccine startup, and planning the launch of revolutionary medicines.
Biotech_Manager.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and strategic thinking make you perfect for Healthcare Management, Entrepreneurship, or Product Management.
Biotech_Manager.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Science (PCB/PCM) or Commerce with Math. Degree: B.Tech/B.Sc Biotechnology or BBA. Next Steps: Crack CAT -> MBA in Healthcare or Biotech Management.
